clue.text: Host seems clever occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so take every other letter of the two words, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A party host comes across as rather bright now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Starting from the second letter of 'seems', every other letter through 'clever' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the person who presents and hosts an event or show.

clue.text: Look into flights to find cuts

indicators.note: into means placed within, so the word for look goes inside

parts.note: escapes are flights, as in fleeing
lo is an old word meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: Someone examines flight options to find cheaper fares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flights' suggests planes or stairs, but it means escapes, as in taking flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalopes are thin slices of boneless meat, cuts beaten flat for frying.

clue.text: Official swore no rock climbing — after fragments fall off

indicators.note: climbing in a down answer means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed
when the bits at either end break away, a run of letters inside these words is left

explanation.surface: A climber swears off rock climbing after loose pieces fall away.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'swore no rock' sits RENOROC; reading it upwards, as 'climbing' directs, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is a public official who holds inquests into sudden or suspicious deaths.

clue.text: Time's against goddess

parts.note: an era is a period of time; the 's means is
to can mean against, as in leaning the door to or setting a ladder to a wall

explanation.surface: The clock is ticking against a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: ERA plus TO. The 's of 'Time's' is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the divine patron of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Small white ball dropping behind a golf club's tree

indicators.note: dropping its behind means the ball's word loses its final letter

parts.note: the jack is the small white ball bowled at in the game of bowls
the R and A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, golf's old governing body

explanation.surface: A little white golf ball drops behind a club member's tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small white ball' sounds like golf, but it is the jack from lawn bowls. The R and A (Royal and Ancient) is the St Andrews club that long governed golf.
explanation.definitionFit: The jacaranda is a tropical American tree known for its clusters of blue-violet flowers.

clue.text: Oddly blue joke cracked by Greek characters on island originally cast as locals for Mamma Mia?

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so the pooled letters are rearranged
oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first and third

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram pool
x means by, as in a room measured 3 x 4
mu is a Greek letter, so mus are more than one

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of each of the words around it

explanation.surface: A rude gag is broken by Greek actors on an island, cast as natives for the film of the Abba show.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange BU (odd letters of blue) and JOKE to get JUKEBO; then X (by), MUS, and ICAL from the first letters of island, cast, as, locals.
explanation.definitionFit: A jukebox musical strings together existing pop hits; Mamma Mia! is built from Abba songs, the best-known example.

clue.text: Bohemians sounded angry at first before journalist provided means of payment

indicators.note: before means the word for angry comes ahead of the journalist
at first means this pair comes first, ahead of the word said aloud

parts.note: cross means angry
ED is short for editor, a crossword stock journalist

indicators.note: sounded means spoken, so the word for Bohemians is replaced by one pronounced alike

parts.note: Bohemia is part of the Czech Republic, so Bohemians are Czechs

explanation.surface: Some Bohemians spoke up angrily before a reporter offered to cover the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'Czechs' matches the plural of the British spelling of bank cheques.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossed cheques have two parallel lines drawn across them so they can only be paid into a bank account, a form of payment.

clue.text: Told about, say, going down

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for told surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: related means told, as of a story
eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: Someone was told about, for instance, sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a relegated team goes down a division, which is why the definition fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A relegated team has been sent down to a lower division, so it is going down at the season's end.

clue.text: Lumps somehow led us on

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A doctor somehow strung us along about the lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of LED US ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodules are small rounded swellings or growths, such as those found in tissue.

clue.text: Fix rotating handle — starter for double-decker

indicators.note: rotating means turning round, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

indicators.note: starter for means the opening letter of double-decker

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a turning handle on a London bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a knob, but it means a name; NAME rotated becomes AMEN, then add D.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to correct or improve it, which is what fixing it means.

clue.text: New Age crank largely dwells on it

indicators.note: new here means made anew, so the letters that follow are put into a fresh order
largely means most of it, so the last letter of dwells is cut off

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram pool

explanation.surface: An eccentric New Age type keeps going on about the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' reads as one phrase, but 'New' is the anagram signal and 'Age' is fodder. Rearrange AGE, CRANK, DWELL (dwells, most of it) and ON. 'It' is a common euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal knowledge is a legal and old-fashioned phrase for sexual intercourse, which 'it' coyly stands for.

clue.text: Pound put on black — splitting responsibility — it's normally red

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: splitting means the two pieces before it break the word for responsibility apart and sit inside it

parts.note: an onus is a duty or responsibility
to don clothes is to put them on
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gambler puts a pound on black at roulette, sharing the risk — though red usually wins.
explanation.walkthrough: The roulette picture makes 'red' look like a colour on the wheel; it is the definition of a London bus, whose famous double-deckers are red.
explanation.definitionFit: London's buses, especially the double-deckers, are famously painted red, so the description fits the vehicle.

clue.text: Cold — Geordie's content to go out with top on

indicators.note: the inner letters, its content, are removed, leaving only the first and last

parts.note: the word Geordie, with the 's meaning has; a Geordie is someone from Tyneside in north-east England
a lid is a top on a container

explanation.surface: A Tynesider is happy to head outdoors in the cold with a hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy', but it means the contents: empty GEORDIE to leave GE. A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid is a literary adjective for icy or freezing, from the Latin word for frost.

clue.text: Confuse electorate — making nothing right with vote

indicators.note: making nothing right means the zero in the word becomes the letter for right

parts.note: the people are the voters, the electorate
O looks like zero, nothing
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: Voters are left baffled when a ballot achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In PEOPLE, swap the O (nothing) for R (right) to give PERPLE, then add X for a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To perplex someone is to puzzle or bewilder them, a synonym of confuse.

clue.text: Like some tea gents? On vacation smoke marijuana

parts.note: the gents is a men's toilet, a loo

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: leaf is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Some men take a holiday break for tea and a cannabis smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: A gents is the British term for a men's toilet. Emptying SMOKE leaves SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose-leaf tea is sold as unbagged dried leaves rather than in tea bags.

clue.text: Milk supplier's entertaining second commercial sent over computer file

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, so everything is read backwards
entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a teat supplies milk; the 's means is
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A dairy farm emails an advert to a client as an attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk supplier' wants to be a dairy or cow; it is the teat. Everything, the commercial included, is reversed by 'sent over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A data set is a collection of related data held together, which in computing is stored as a file.

clue.text: Urgent supply to prop up country wanting vital piece of military hardware

indicators.note: to prop up means to sit beneath, so the anagram comes below in the down answer
wanting means lacking, so the vital piece is removed

parts.note: Turkey is a country
a key piece is a vital one

indicators.note: supply here means supple, pliant, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: An urgent delivery to support a country short of a vital weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun for deliveries, but it is the adverb of supple, signalling rearrangement. TURKEY without KEY is TUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A turret gun is a heavy weapon mounted in a rotating turret on a tank or warship.

clue.text: Space after group of students returned to conservatory?

indicators.note: after means the word for space comes later than the reversed piece
returned means sent back, so the students' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
room means space

explanation.surface: Students come back from a term away to find more space in the conservatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students. The question mark admits a conservatory is only one kind of sun room.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory is a glazed room built onto a house to let in sunlight, an example of a sun room.

clue.text: Reformed character inspiring son to become journalist

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the son goes inside

parts.note: a new man is someone who has changed his ways, a reformed character
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A former villain who encourages his son to go into journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like encouraging, but it means breathing in, holding the son inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a reporter or other journalist who gathers and writes the news.

clue.text: See 4
TV channel invested in vehicle — something 2 might study

indicators.note: invested in means clothed by, so the channel's name sits inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Dave is a British comedy television channel

explanation.surface: A broadcaster pours money into a car, which an official might investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is the answer to 2-down, CORONER. Dave is a UK channel showing comedy repeats.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner investigates sudden or unexplained deaths, so a dead body is what they examine.

clue.text: See 5
Virginia creeper not against supporting walls for clinic offering jab?

indicators.note: supporting means holding up from below, so the creeper part sits under the walls in the down answer

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: walls for means the outer letters, the walls, of clinic
not means without, so the letter for against is taken out

parts.note: a vine is a creeping plant
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Virginia creeper is no barrier against clinic walls offering an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia creeper' reads as the plant's name, but the two words work separately. 'Supporting' puts the trimmed creeper beneath the clinic's walls in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine is usually given by injection, informally a jab in British English, so the question mark marks a typical delivery.

clue.text: Pop star's dicky heart finally giving way

indicators.note: giving way means yielding its place, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a dicky bow is British slang for a bow tie

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of heart

explanation.surface: A singer's weak heart finally fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like 'unreliable', describing the heart; it is the British word for a bow tie. Remove T (heart's last letter) from BOWTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: David Bowie was a hugely influential English pop and rock singer and songwriter.

clue.text: Book written by an American student's trite

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A book written by a US student is unoriginal.
explanation.walkthrough: A learner driver in Britain displays an L plate, so L stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means dull through overuse or lacking originality, the same as trite.

clue.text: Cancels pet's treatment — having Alsatian's tail docked for show

indicators.note: treatment means handling or working over, so the letters are rearranged
docked, as with a dog's tail, means a letter is cut from the pool
the tail of the dog's name is its final letter, the one docked

explanation.surface: An owner calls off a pet's treatment because the Alsatian has had its tail docked.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of CANCELS PET, remove the N that ends 'Alsatian', and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking display or performance put on for an audience, a synonym of show.

clue.text: It's understood I whip up dessert at the end

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

indicators.note: at the end picks the last letter of dessert

explanation.surface: A cook makes it plain they will whisk up a pudding at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip up' reads as whisking cream; but 'whip' is CAT and 'up' reverses I and CAT to TACI, then add T. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or unspoken, so a tacit agreement is understood without being stated.

clue.text: Critical point during surgery — essentially resting on anaesthetist's complex calculations

indicators.note: resting on means sitting after the anaesthetist's word in the across answer

parts.note: an anaesthetist numbs patients, so is jokingly a number (one who numbs)
the crunch is the crucial or decisive moment
in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, the central letter of surgery

explanation.surface: At the decisive moment of an operation, a team depends on the anaesthetist's tricky dosage sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' must be read as one who numbs, rhyming with 'plumber', not as a figure. 'Surgery' has seven letters, so its essence is the single middle G.
explanation.definitionFit: Number-crunching is informal for doing large or complicated mathematical calculations, typically by computer.

clue.text: Gets over charge for tips

indicators.note: over means covering, so the word for gets goes round the word for charge

parts.note: to land something is to get or secure it
to fill, as a glass or a pipe, is to charge it

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from being billed for advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' reads as advice or gratuities; in Britain a tip is also a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A landfill is a site where waste is buried, called a rubbish tip in British English.

clue.text: That is breaking metal connection

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the abbreviation goes inside the metal

parts.note: tin is a metal
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A metal link is snapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is the phrase spelled out by the Latin abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a link or association between things, such as a product connected to a film.
